answer: Posted collateral must equal 4 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. Because the lagoon collateral is checked against the comet claim at intake, the nadir audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases thus has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
